# Introduction

You can build a well-structured and maintainable layout, by using these main layout components: `Main`, `Section` and `Grid`. These components allow for consistent styling and layout management, making the development process more efficient.

## General page layout

This example contains the available layout components. Let's breakdown the page from top to bottom level.

## Main

The `Main` component is responsible for grouping sections and makes it scrollable when you add more sections to this component. This will be rendered as **`<main />`** tag on Web. This is also a virtualized list component, which gives you additional options such as the configuring the rendering behavior of the `Section` items.

## Section

A Section component is typically used to define distinct sections of a webpage. It helps in creating a structured layout. It ensures consistent vertical spacing between the major parts of your page content, creating a clear sense of hierarchy and separation. Next to that it has options to specify a `title`, `subTitle`, `image`, `description` text and call-to-action buttons (`triggers`), see illustrated example below (these are optional fields).

## Grid

A `Grid` component is used to center content and constrain its maximum width, ensuring consistent spacing and alignment. See the example below. The properties like `title`, `subtitle`, `triggers` and `description` set within `Section` will horizontally align to the options set in the first `Grid` child. For example, if you set the `variant` property to `narrow`, the title of the `Section` will update accordingly.

The `Grid` also offers you the option to set the column width (1 to 12) for each of the `Grid.Column`. You can also do this per breakpoint. For example, you would apply a column width of 6 on breakpoint `tablet` and a column width of 12 on breakpoint `mobileSmall`. The columns will take up a 50/50 split on tablet (and up), and take up 100% width on the mobileSmall (up to tablet) breakpoint.

## Grid.Column

A `Grid.Column` component is used to contain components. Much like the `Grid`, you also have the option to set the width of the column (1 to 12), either per breakpoint, or across all breakpoints. Added advantage here is that you have the option to set variable widths for each column within the `Grid`.

## Stack

The Stack component is a flex component with additional flexbox properties. It simplifies creating flexible layouts with various alignment and justification options. For example if you want to change the direction of the items inside a Stack component you can change the direction property (vertical/horizontal). Like the `Grid` component you also have the option to set `Stack` properties for each breakpoint, or you could have different values for each breakpoint.

## Box

The Box component is a simple wrapper that has various styles. It's useful for creating a consistent interface with spacing, background colors, borders.
